newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine PM urges parliament to pass new tax laws.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine PM urges parliament to pass new tax laws.

text.p: Ukraine's Prime Minister Pavlo Lazarenko told deputies on Thursday that passing tax reform laws early in the new year would lead to growth in gross domestic product in 1997.
"If the tax laws are not accepted, GDP will fall four percent in 1997, and 3.8 percent in 1998," Lazarenko said.
Lazarenko urged parliament to approve the 1997 draft budget, which includes the new tax laws, in mid-January or February.
The government handed parliament the proposed tax laws and the draft budget in November, and Lazarenko said the budget could not realistically be implemented without new tax laws.
The prime minister said the laws would bring a significant portion of Ukraine's large shadow economy into the light.
The current tax regime has been blamed for forcing many businesses, which can pay more than 100 percent of profits in tax, into the shadow economy.
The new tax laws will lower tax rates by broadening the tax base.
Lazarenko also said Ukraine could no longer afford to pay the huge quantity of social benefits paid to citizens in the Soviet era.
Parliament earlier this month gave a first reading to the draft budget, a combination of two budgets proposed by the government earlier plus changes suggested by parliamentarians.
The economy is forecast to experience modest growth in 1997, its first year of growth in the post-Soviet era.
